caption:
This planet orbits its star backwards.
Astronomy & Astrophysics, Sept 2026; arXiv 2609.24870. Carteret, University of Geneva; NIRPS, La Silla.

GJ 3090 b, 73 light-years away, orbits its red dwarf tilted about 136 degrees: past sideways, into backwards. 2.2 Earth radii, 4.5 Earth masses, a 2.9-day year. First retrograde planet found around a red dwarf; no known companion. What flipped it?

#exoplanet #astronomy #space #science
voiceover_script: There is a planet orbiting its star backwards, and tilted. Every planet in our solar system goes round in the same direction the Sun spins. This one does not. G J three zero nine zero b sits seventy three light-years away, around a red dwarf star. It is about two point two times Earth's radius, four and a half times its mass, and its year lasts two point nine days. Its orbit is tilted about one hundred and thirty six degrees: past sideways, into backwards. It is the first retrograde planet found around a red dwarf, and no known companion explains how it got there.
